summary: Music Business Worldwide's Tim Ingham interviews Michelle Jubelirer on her first two years as Chair and CEO of Capitol Music Group (CMG), after leadership turmoil under Jeff Vaughn. She credits a rebuilt culture, artist-specific campaigns, early international engagement and a push into hip-hop and R&B for the turnaround, citing Ice Spice, Sam Smith's Unholy, Doechii and The Beatles' Now And Then. She also covers the Virgin Music and Motown restructurings and calls for more diversity in the industry.
one_line: Capitol Music Group chief Michelle Jubelirer explains how she stabilized and revived the label group in under two years, with Ice Spice, Sam Smith and The Beatles.
key_facts: Michelle Jubelirer was named Chair and CEO of Capitol Music Group after Jeff Vaughn left within about 12 months of succeeding Steve Barnett in December 2020.
CMG's US market share year-to-date is in the high-5% region, and Jubelirer says year-over-year market share is up 25% with CMG moving up a notch in the label rankings.

Ice Spice, a Best New Artist Grammy nominee, has four Top 10 Billboard Hot 100 singles and over 2 billion global streams from her debut EP; she is signed to CMG in partnership with Elliot Grainge's 10K Projects.
Ice Spice is the first artist since Olivia Rodrigo to achieve three Top 5 single debuts in her first four months, according to Jubelirer.

Doechii's What It Is (Block Boy) is platinum in the US, has passed 1.1 billion worldwide streams, and was TikTok's fourth biggest global track of 2023; it spread via TikTok in Nigeria, Kenya, the Philippines and Douyin in China, reaching 1.5 million daily creates.
The Beatles' Now And Then, released by CMG in November 2023, hit No.1 in multiple territories including the UK, Germany and Austria; Jubelirer signed Paul McCartney directly to Capitol in 2016.
Capitol was the top-performing label across TikTok's global and US end-of-year lists in 2023.
Motown was spun out of CMG in early 2021 and returned to CMG in early 2023; CMG is still searching for a new leader for Motown.
Caroline/Virgin Music was spun out of CMG to form Virgin Music Group, led by President Jacqueline Saturn.
Quality Control, Motown's JV partner since 2015, was sold to Scooter Braun-led HYBE America for $300 million in February 2023, while Warner Music Group acquired 51% of 10K Projects in September 2023.
Ice Spice was carved out of 10K's Warner deal and remains signed in partnership with CMG.
Jubelirer's priorities included signing diverse new artists with a focus on hip-hop and R&B, restructuring the organization, and tailoring every plan to a specific artist rather than a set playbook.
CMG's labels include Blue Note, Motown, Priority, Astralwerks, Capitol Christian and Tamla.
Jubelirer wants more diversity across the industry, noting that Cindy Mabe and she are the only women running standalone label groups at UMG.
